question: An IT service desk is updating the onboarding slide it uses to explain how staff conversations relate to model training. Which two statements are accurate to put on the slide? Select two.
options: A) Switching model improvement on applies it to every conversation already in the user's account.
B) Work done in the company's Claude for Work account is not used to train models by default.
C) Personal Free and Pro accounts are also excluded from model training by default, as Work is too.
D) Deleting a conversation immediately removes every copy of it from all of Anthropic's systems.
E) Incognito chats are never used to improve Claude, whatever the account's other settings say.
correct_answers: B) Work done in the company's Claude for Work account is not used to train models by default.
E) Incognito chats are never used to improve Claude, whatever the account's other settings say.
explanations: Enabling the setting applies only to new or resumed chats after it is turned on; it does not reach back over untouched past conversations.
Correct. On commercial offerings, including Claude for Work, inputs and outputs are not used for model training by default.
Consumer plans work the other way round: the user chooses, so training is a setting rather than an automatic exclusion.
Deletion is not instantaneous everywhere, and some material is retained for safety and legal purposes, so this would mislead staff.
Correct, and for a separate reason: the incognito exclusion is absolute and does not depend on how the model improvement setting is configured.
